summary:
We developed Mission: Save Ash, user friendly and interactive 10-day survival simulation. Players take the role of an astronaut left alone on the Moon with limited resources that keeps him breathing. The game challenges players to balance resources: oxygen, power, food, and health, while reacting to unpredictable lunar crisis that can happen at any sudden moment.		
Players tackle some of the authentic space threats, such as Dust Strom, Solar Radiations, Food, Power, and lack of Oxygen, and communication with earth is disrupted. These threats are incorporated with authentic geographical details: Taurus-Littrow valley and Lunar Reconnaissance data, keeping the survival scenario scientifically accurate. It also tackles the psychological and physical strain of long-duration in space forcing players to balance the life support essentials.

This project matters because it proves and emphasis that space exploration isn’t just about rocket and science, instead shows how to be calm under pressure, and take right decisions at the right time to survive. By managing limited resources and solve sudden crisis, it helps children sharpen their decision making, and critical thinking in a way they can apply to their daily lives. Other than that this simulation turns complex lunar data, and space threats into an interactive experience that anyone can understand and enjoy
details:
Mission: Rescue Ash


Our solution to the challenge— Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer—is an interactive choice based game that we named Mission: Rescue Ash.

Storyline

You play as the character Ash, Who is on a Lunar Mission. Your lander is wrecked and your crew is gone. You are alone in an emergency base near the Taurus-Littrow valley, where long-lived quakes shake the ground and the only protection from radiation is your own walls.

Rescue arrives on day 10. Until then every choice costs you something. Oxygen, power and food drain daily, and his body shows it. Watch his face and his vitals. Let any one hit zero for too long and you won’t make it.

Details

As you begin, you are given choices. Each choice has its pros and cons. You decide which decision would be beneficial in that particular scenario.

Each day, you use up your resources such as oxygen, food and power. You also encounter random major events such as a dust storm, moonquakes, food spoilage and oxygen leakage. In each of these major events, your choices affect your resources directly. Your decisions manipulate the Characters moral as well. Every night you are also given a choice that includes: consuming food for health, scavenging outside for resources, or going straight to sleep.

Technical details

We developed the game using python and html. The process we followed was that we planned our events and all the choices first. Then we implemented the events in python and made a rough text only draft for the game with no visuals, and js buttons and labels using the python library 'tkinter', we refined our logic and began debugging. We used SI for debugging errors that we couldn't figure out.

After we had our code, we used Vs Studio to develop the code into a html project that can run on a browser.

For the graphical user interface and art for the game, we used PicsArt, Claude, MS Paint.

How 'Mission: Rescue Ash' helps young minds.


The Game was specifically designed in a way so that young and future astronauts dont get overwhelmed with so many factors to keep track of, while still making sure the stakes felt high and real. It gives the players free will to choose their decisions and see their choices play out in real time. Each option they choose matters. Every decision leads to either success or failure of the mission.

We hoped to create a game where kids learn the power of their choice and how each little decision affects everything around them. It helps improve their problem solving skills and aspires them to learn and grow, while offering a little bit of fun along the way!

We made sure that the game wasn't too hard for the kids and it wasn't too boring. It features a voice over that u can turn on and off, which helps kids with audio aid. It includes calm synth background music. We made the game keeping in mind replayability and not overwhelming kids with too many factors and resources to keep track of. We made it a bit challenging so that not only kids but astronauts of all ages can play and learn.
